title: Evaluation of the stabilizing effect and fit of a semi-flexible, individually adjustable four-point knee brace in patients after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
summary:
This study investigates how well two different knee braces stabilize the knee and how well they fit and are tolerated in everyday use in patients after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction. A semi-flexible, individually adjustable knee brace is compared with a conventional rigid-frame knee brace.

After informed consent, participants are randomly assigned to one of the two brace groups. A first assessment is performed before surgery. At this time point, patients are assessed without a brace and with both braces. After surgery, all patients receive standard postoperative care. From the third postoperative week onwards, they wear the assigned knee brace according to the established clinical treatment protocol. A second assessment is performed approximately three to four weeks after surgery.

During the assessments, participants perform several standardized movement tasks. Patients walk overground at their individually preferred walking speed. In addition, they perform a turning task including 90° and 180° turning manoeuvres. Furthermore, they walk on a treadmill both at their individually determined habitual walking speed and at a standardized speed of 1.11 m/s. During these tasks, knee joint motion, ground reaction forces, and muscle activity are recorded.

The aim of the study is to evaluate whether the semi-flexible brace provides comparable or improved stabilization, fit, and usability in daily life compared with the rigid-frame brace. For contextual comparison of gait parameters, reference data from healthy participants obtained from an existing gait database will be used. No separate healthy control group will be recruited prospectively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• ACL rupture with indication for surgical treatment
• Age between 18 and 60 years
• Physically active individuals participating in occasional sports activities, defined as Tegner Activity Scale ≥3
• Healthy contralateral limb*
• Patients who receive the same postoperative treatment protocol due to comparable severity and type of injury and surgical procedure

* The contralateral limb is considered healthy if the non-operated lower extremity has had no acute injury, no surgery, no relevant pain, and no musculoskeletal or neurological complaints within the previous six months that could affect gait or the performance of the measurement tasks.
Exclusion criteria:
• Injury of the posterior cruciate ligament
• Medial knee instability > grade I according to Hughston
• Neurological disorders or other comorbidities that may affect gait
